description: The Penn State Smeal Master of Accounting (MAcc) Program offers two paths to a graduate degree and the 150 credit hours required to be a CPA: The Integrated MAcc Program and the One-Year MAcc Program. The program provides the specialized knowledge and professional skills needed for success in the accounting profession, preparing students for the challenges of the profession and meeting the requirements for CPA licensure in most states. Smeal accounting graduates are highly sought after by top accounting firms and corporations, gaining technical knowledge necessary for success in public accounting, corporate accounting, and other related fields.

description: The Penn State Smeal College of Business is merging its two one-year accounting master’s programs — the Master of Science in Accounting Analytics (MAA) and the Master of Accounting (MAcc) — to create a single, comprehensive program: the Master of Science in Accounting Analytics. Starting in fall 2024, the new MAA curriculum will integrate coursework focused on data analytics and technology skills with traditional accounting courses. The curriculum is designed to equip students with the necessary skills to navigate the evolving landscape of the accounting profession and meet the increasing demand for professionals with expertise in data-driven decision-making. The program will offer one-year master’s students two paths to CPA licensure: a non-business path for students with a non-accounting background and an accounting path for those with a bachelor’s degree in accounting. As part of the program, students will participate in a three-credit immersion experience, working in teams to address a real-world accounting analytics problem. They also will gain exposure to emerging technologies like blockchain, artificial intelligence and robotic process automation. The MAA program is STEM-designated and prepares students for the CPA exam.
Program name: Master of Science in Accounting Analytics
Program Page url: https://www.psu.edu/news/smeal-college-business/story/penn-state-smeal-merge-accounting-analytics-master-accounting-program

description: The graduate program in economics at Penn State is designed for students interested in obtaining a Ph.D. in economics. The program is centered on the University Park campus, which is the largest of Penn State’s campuses and is home to most of the University’s research and graduate programs. The primary goal of the program is to provide students with the skills they need to conduct original research in economics. The first year of the program is devoted to core courses in microeconomic theory, macroeconomic theory, and econometrics. In the second year, students begin to specialize in one or more of the department’s many fields of strength, which include: econometrics, industrial organization, international economics, macroeconomics, microeconomic theory, and development economics. Students also begin to work on their own research projects in the second year, often in collaboration with faculty members. The M.A. degree in economics is only available to students who are already enrolled in the Ph.D. program. The M.A. degree may be awarded as an interim degree for students in the Ph.D. program or if the student terminates study before completing the Ph.D. requirements.

description:
The Master of Professional Studies (M.P.S.) in Quality and Manufacturing Management (QMM) is a 32-credit degree program. It is an online, interdisciplinary, professional master’s degree, provided by the College of Engineering and the Smeal College of Business. The QMM program provides an opportunity for students to study the fundamental principles of manufacturing and quality systems. Students learn to apply the technical and business skills needed to manage the design, production, and delivery of products and services. The M.P.S. degree is a unique combination of engineering and business topics, providing students with the skills and knowledge to lead the development of world-class, integrated manufacturing and service businesses. 

Educational Objectives:
1. The program graduates will lead the design, development, and improvement of manufacturing and service systems.
2. The program graduates will apply technical and business skills to evaluate and improve the quality of manufacturing and service processes.
3. The program graduates will evaluate manufacturing and service businesses as integrated systems of engineering and business functions.
4. The program graduates will utilize effective leadership and communication skills to work in multidisciplinary teams.

Student Learning Outcomes:
1. Communicate (in writing and orally) to a variety of audiences.
2. Work effectively in multidisciplinary teams.
3. Use technical and business skills to manage and improve manufacturing and service processes.
4. Analyze manufacturing and service businesses as integrated systems of engineering and business functions.
5. Explain and use the fundamental principles of manufacturing and quality systems.

description: The Graduate Certificate in Additive Manufacturing and Design program is designed to educate students and working engineers in the analytical and practical methods for the design and manufacturing of devices utilizing additive manufacturing. Additive manufacturing (AM) is a suite of emerging technologies that fabricate three-dimensional objects directly from digital models through the repeated addition of material. AM provides a new design paradigm, allowing for the creation of components with unprecedented levels of complexity and/or parts that are produced locally and on-demand. The program is designed to provide students with a foundational knowledge in the entire AM workflow, including the design, materials, and processing of AM parts. The program is a multidisciplinary program with faculty from the College of Engineering and the College of Earth and Mineral Sciences. As such, the program provides a unique opportunity to integrate various aspects of AM, including design, and the materials and processing of AM parts, to ensure students are provided with the most comprehensive AM education.
Program name: Graduate Credit Certificate in Additive Manufacturing and Design

description: The Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner (AGACNP) graduate credit certificate program is designed for the master's-prepared nurse practitioner who has at least one year of experience in an acute care setting and is looking to pivot into an acute care role. This certificate program provides master’s-prepared nurse practitioners with the necessary knowledge and skills to provide advanced nursing care to adult and gerontology patients in acute care settings. The curriculum emphasizes the assessment, diagnosis, and management of acute and chronic conditions, as well as the promotion of health and prevention of disease in this population. The certificate program consists of 18 credits of study and 500 hours of supervised clinical practice in an acute care setting. Upon completion of the program, students will be eligible to sit for the Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner board certification exam through the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC) or the American Association of Critical-Care Nurses (AACN).
Accreditation status: The post-graduate APRN certificate programs at The Pennsylvania State University are accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE).
Program name: Graduate Credit Certificate in Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner

description: The Graduate Credit Certificate in Adult Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioner (AGPCNP) is designed for the nurse who has already earned a master’s degree in nursing and is seeking to expand their knowledge and clinical skills to provide primary care to the adult population (ages 13 to end-of-life). description: The Graduate Certificate in Geospatial Intelligence Analytics is designed to prepare the next generation of geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) professionals to work in the national security community, the private sector, and international organizations. GEOINT is the branch of intelligence that involves the use and analysis of imagery and geospatial information to describe, assess, and visually depict physical features and geographically referenced activities on the Earth. The program focuses on the development of critical thinking and analytical skills through the application of geospatial technologies to complex, real-world problems. The certificate program is intended for students who are currently working in or who wish to enter the geospatial intelligence field.
Accreditation status: The Graduate Certificate in Geospatial Intelligence Analytics is accredited by the United States Geospatial Intelligence Foundation (USGIF).

description: The Graduate Credit Certificate in Translational Science is designed to provide a targeted and concise program for clinical and translational research training for students who are looking for such training but who do not have the time to commit to the M.S. in Public Health Sciences or the Ph.D. in Biomedical Sciences or other doctoral degree programs. This certificate program will focus on the principles of translational science, which is a multidisciplinary field that focuses on the translation of basic research into clinical practice. It is expected that the Certificate will meet a current need for a shorter, more specific program for clinical and translational research training for students such as medical students, residents, and fellows. Students in the certificate program will learn the basics of clinical research, including the design and conduct of clinical trials, the analysis of clinical data, and the ethics of clinical research. They will also learn about the regulatory process for the development of new medical treatments and the translation of basic research into clinical practice.
Program name: Graduate Credit Certificate in Translational Science
